Morning in the little town. The bakery is already smoking, the cobbles are still wet, and on the corner stands a booth nobody wanted.
A cart rolls up with one coin at the bottom. A capybara peeks out. Looks confident. Mostly.
Hello, booth. I'm Capy. One coin, lots of plans, and no backup.
The roof leaks, the sign hangs crooked, but there's an awning. I'll call it “Everything for a Penny”. The penny is already here.
They say whoever stands on the corner sees the whole town. Nobody warned me the whole town would see me.
The first customer is already shuffling by the door, clutching a purse. Time to tap: every touch is a coin.
A few days in, the till rings so much that Capy can't keep up with selling or counting. A hedgehog with a piece of paper has been sitting by the door for ages.
Good day. Any openings? I'm Spike. I can count, I can't steal. Mostly don't want to.
But you're prickly. Customers are probably scared.
The honest ones aren't scared. The others aren't either, but they regret it later.
The till is yours. No trial period: we have neither the time nor the money.
Thanks. Not a single penny will get lost. Unless it gets stuck in the quills. Then I'll definitely return it.
Tip: open the “Team” tab and hire Spike. He boosts your tap power.
With Spike at the till, business took off and the whole town heard about the shop. Along with the customers came someone who didn't plan to pay.
Capy! A pack of cookies is gone. I only caught a striped tail and a very confident back.
Striped tail. Confident back. There's only one of those in this neighbourhood.
No offence, it isn't stealing, it's freelance. I'm Shnyr, the fastest raccoon on this street.
That's my cookie. Give it back. Now.
It's been... slightly tasted. Call it a review. And now, no catching me!
Gone. I told you we need a safe. Even a small one.
The raccoon is sly, but doesn't seem mean. He'll be back. Better hide valuables, and nerves too.
Hiding valuables from the raccoon, Capy rummages through the stockroom and finds something odd in a corner.
A pocket watch. The gold has darkened, the glass is cracked. Old, but with character.
It ticks. But the hands go backwards. Definitely not by the manual.
Broken. My grandpa said: a watch that runs backwards is either broken or has a surprise.
I don't like surprises. But it's pretty. I'll keep it, no warranty.
In the pocket the watch ticked softly, as if winking. Looks like that wasn't the last time.
The shop has grown into a supermarket. The whole street talks about Capy, and new workers are knocking on the door. Those who could, knocked.
I'm Bodya, a builder. Heard you're expanding. Need boards? I'll send the bill separately. And another one, for politeness.
Zoya. I sell everything that isn't nailed down. And what is nailed down, just slower. Give me a window and it'll start talking.
Hoo. I'm Sonia, an accountant. I work nights, by day I only blink. Someone has to count these coins before they run away.
Tonya, security. I'm coming. Will be there soon. But I won't let anyone through.
Come in, friends. Thank you for coming. Seriously.
Thanks are nice. But I haven't seen how the bonus question ends.
